notes:
- The trailer plays inside the app: Tapping the trailer card used to hand the video to a browser and lose the title you were reading. It opens a player over the page now, with the escape hatch of opening it on YouTube underneath if a video is region-locked.
- The score sits in a wavy ring: The score on a title's summary strip is drawn inside the page's own wave, closed into a ring, and fills to the share of 100 the score is. The other three numbers stay plain figures, because a ring around a popularity count would be a picture of a measurement nobody took.
- Waiting for a score turns the wave round: Where the strip used to shimmer over a number that did not exist yet, the score cell now waits as the loading mark - the same wavy ring, with a short accent arc travelling around it. It stops when the page is in the background or the reader has asked for Instant motion.
- Numbers roll instead of flickering: A value in the summary strip cross-faded in place, so two numbers of different widths made the row twitch sideways while it changed. They roll now, up and out and in from below, on the same spring the app's counters use.
- A bio with live card images scrolls like a picture: The stat cards and banners people put in their AniList bios are drawn by a web engine, and holding one of those open for every card made a decorated profile stutter while it scrolled - the app was rebuilding the whole engine each time the bio came back into view. Each card is now drawn once and kept as a picture, so scrolling it costs the same as scrolling a photo. An animated banner stops animating, which is the trade.
- Posters show their titles before their art: Every cover now draws the title's initials on a tint of its own before the artwork arrives, and keeps them if the picture never loads. A cold start used to be a grid of identical grey boxes - or, on the Home rails, holes where the cover had no colour - so the first screen now reads as your list rather than as a page still building itself. Nothing is fetched for it: the initials come from the title the app already has.
- Video embeds look like videos: `youtube(…)` and `webm(…)` in a bio now draw a poster card: the video's own frame, a play badge and the address under it, instead of a line of text that said there was a video somewhere else. Tapping opens it, as every other embed in a bio does.
- Discord habits render: `||spoiler||` hides text the way `~!spoiler!~` does, `-# text` draws as quiet subtext and `>>> ` quotes everything after it. These are Discord's forms, not AniList's; a bio that used them showed the punctuation and the secret it was hiding.
- Ratings obey the setting on the Library grid: The reader's own Library page drew the list owner's score on every poster while the design settings said to show the community average, so the same title disagreed with the page it opened. Both grid paths now read the same rule.
- Progress badges are not covered by a heart: On the Modern and Stamp card styles the rating takes the poster's top corner, which moves the progress pill to the other one - where the pinned-favourite mark was already drawn, on top of the number. The two now share that corner instead of hiding each other.
- Chapter counts get a book, not a play button: A manga poster's progress pill wore the same play triangle as an episode count. It now draws the book mark beside "Ch 42/50".
- A formatter that posted literal tags is gone: The comment composer's Underline button wrote `<u>…</u>`, which AniList strips: the tag travelled to the comment as text. The site has no underline, so the button is removed rather than left to post markup.
- The Stats tab says when a count is missing: Four of its charts are tallied from the media list, and a list that failed to load left them empty with no note - "Nothing recorded yet" over an account with hundreds of entries. A failing list now says so and states which charts are unaffected.
- "Show hidden" counts the list you are looking at: The pill added the hidden rows of both inbox halves together and appeared on any filter, so Sent could offer "Hidden (3)" with nothing behind it. The count and the pill now follow the selected filter and the rows actually loaded.
- Refresh no longer leaves the manga half behind: The profile's Refresh button re-read the anime half of a borrowed list and every feed that was open, but not the manga list, so pulling to refresh a stranger's Manga grid could not be done from the bar above it.
- "Finished 1 entries" is gone: The Watch Year chart's subtitle singularises a single finished title, the way the episode note beside it already did.
- Smaller controls are now big enough to hit: The Library's type and sort chips were 40dp tall while every other chip in the app uses 44dp, which is what makes them reliable on a phone held one-handed.
